headline: This law delays until January 3, 2015, a deadline for the Transportation Department to post pipeline safety reference documents free online, and it loosens how those documents must be made public.
what_it_does: Pipeline safety rules often refer to outside technical documents, a practice called incorporation by reference. Before this law, DOT could adopt those documents only if they were posted free on a public website, with a deadline of January 3, 2012. This law moves that deadline to January 3, 2015. It also removes the rule that limited public availability to internet posting and drops a bar on issuing guidance when those requirements are not met.

who_it_affects.how: The timing and method for making referenced pipeline safety documents public changes, which affects the standards they must follow.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the public who want to read pipeline safety standards
who_it_affects.how: Referenced documents no longer have to be available only on the internet, which changes how they can be accessed.

who_it_affects.group: Department of Transportation pipeline safety staff
who_it_affects.how: They receive more time and flexibility in publishing referenced documents and issuing guidance.

when_it_takes_effect: Upon enactment on August 9, 2013, with the revised deadline of January 3, 2015.
